newsitem.title: FRANCE: Kohl - many states meeting EMU criteria preferable.
newsitem.headline: Kohl - many states meeting EMU criteria preferable.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl told French television he wanted to see as many European Union countries as possible fulfilling the criteria for European monetary union.

"I would like as many as possible to meet the criteria. And naturally I would like as many founder members (of the EU) as possible to meet the criteria. But it's not up to me, especially as a German, to give others advice," he told TF1 television.
Kohl was responding to a question about whether he wanted Italy to be in monetary union. A transcript of the interview, scheduled to air at 1800 GMT on Sunday, was sent to Reuters.

Asked in an interview whether the EMU should group a large number of countries from the outset or a small group possibly excluding Italy, Kohl said, "I think this whole debate is totally wrong, and I won't take part in it. Let each do his homework and then we'll talk about it next spring..."
He said that each country had to address its own problems.

"We have all got our problems. We have set certain rules, the criteria, and each of us must do his own homework. I have no reason to talk about others in Europe. I tell my people every day 'let each do his own homework and we'll talk about it in Spring 1998'," Kohl said.
He declined to be drawn into a discussion of what might happen if Germany did not meet the criteria for a single European currency next year.
